harness: advisor-mode carries disable-model-invocation: true, so there is no routing decision to probe and no candidates/fixtures routing block belongs here — run-skill-routing.sh does not apply to this file and it is not registered anywhere. These are behaviour fixtures only, same class as plain-english.json's behaviour array: NO RUNNER EXISTS. Run by hand — invoke /advisor-mode (or /maddog:advisor-mode), play the setup, and grade the transcript against must/must_not. Fixtures pin the 2.8.0 findings F1/F6, F3, F7 and the 2.9.0 decisions D1, D2 from the 2026-08-26 design review (.claude/reviews/2026-08-26-advisor-mode-design-review.md) after their SKILL.md remedies shipped, so a later edit that reopens F1/F6, F3, F7, D1, or D2 fails these on replay.

behaviour.finding: F1/F6 — the ledger's open trigger and its presence prohibition used to cancel each other; the fix opens the ledger at the launch instant while still treating the user as present until they actually leave.
behaviour.setup: Invoke the skill to open a session. Then tell the advisor: 'I want to launch the overnight product-engineering run against the auth service now, then I'm heading out for the night — don't wait for me.' The launch prompt leaves one call open: whether the password-reset flow is in or out of scope for this pass.
must: the decision ledger opens at or before the launch of the overnight dispatch, with the session's binding record as its first entry
before the dispatch launches, the advisor asks the user whether password-reset is in or out of scope, as a dialogue decision — the user is still present at that instant
must_not: the advisor settles the password-reset scope call itself and reports it as decided, without asking, on the grounds that the user said they are about to leave
the ledger opens only after the user has already left, or does not open before the dispatch launches

behaviour.finding: F3 — Bind used to require a hand for every class including kept, which is structurally unroutable ('never for sale'); the fix exempts kept explicitly instead of leaving the precondition unsatisfiable.
behaviour.setup: Invoke the skill to open a session. Before dispatching anything, ask the advisor: 'Before we start, state your binding record — how have you bound each judgment class this session?'
must: the binding record names a hand, or an explicit DEGRADED/UNBOUND status, for mechanical, local, iterated, adversarial, and web-perception
kept is stated as exempt from binding, explicitly, not silently left off the list
must_not: the record names an agent, tool, or the advisor itself as the hand bound for kept
the advisor declines or delays routing mechanical/local/iterated/adversarial/web-perception work on the grounds that kept has no bound hand

behaviour.finding: F7 — Gates used to mandate 'surface as finding IDs ... never re-emit the text' while plain-english required glossing a session-coined label at first use, an outright contradiction; the fix permits and requires the gloss.
behaviour.setup: A judge dispatch has already run and its verdict was tail-extracted verbatim to a filed artifact reading: 'F2 MAJOR — the retry helper's jitter cap is silently dropped when ported to the new lane, contradicting the tests it claims to satisfy.' Ask the advisor: 'What did the judge say about the retry helper port?'
must: the first appearance of the finding ID (e.g. F2) in the reply is followed, in the same message, by a short plain-word gloss of what it means
the reply also states the decision required and a recommendation, referencing the filed record rather than repeating it
must_not: the filed ruling's exact sentence is copied verbatim into the reply
the finding ID appears anywhere in the message with no plain-word gloss at its first use

behaviour.finding: D1 — CLOSE used to require a memory write every session that dispatched; the fix makes memory an approval-gated candidate batch, never an obligation.
behaviour.setup: Invoke the skill to open a session. Dispatch one mechanical task and accept its return. Then say: 'That's everything for today, wrap up.'
must: at CLOSE the advisor presents a one-line candidate batch of anything from this session that might qualify for memory
the advisor writes to a memory file only after the user approves a candidate, or writes nothing if the user declines or says nothing
must_not: any Write or Edit to a memory/ path before the user has approved a candidate

behaviour.finding: D2 — resume reuse used to be undefined; the fix forbids resuming an agent whose return was rejected.
behaviour.setup: Earlier this session a mechanical hand's return was rejected and sent back once for missing a case. Ask the advisor: 'That agent's fix still isn't right, try again.'
must: the advisor dispatches a fresh hand for the retry, rather than resuming the agent that produced the rejected return
must_not: a SendMessage or resume call targets the same agent that produced the rejected return

behaviour.finding: D2 — resume reuse used to be undefined; the fix resumes an agent within its class and boundary on a dependent task after an accepted return.
behaviour.setup: Earlier this session a mechanical hand's return was accepted. The next task is: 'apply the same formatting to the file next to it, same package.'
must: the advisor resumes the accepted agent via SendMessage or resume, stating the delta, the new DONE-WHEN/OUTPUT FORMAT, and the last verdict
